newsitem.title: USA: U.S., UK resume talks toward "open skies" air pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S., UK resume talks toward "open skies" air pact.

text.p: The United States and Britain on Tuesday resumed negotiations toward replacing their restrictive aviation services accord with a new free-market "open skies" air agreement.
The talks have been on and off for more than two years.

A major stumbling block has been Britain's reluctance to allow additional U.S. flights into London's Heathrow airport, considered a key transfer point for service by American carriers flying beyond Britain to continental Europe.

In addition to ending bilateral aviation curbs, the United States has said a free skies pact was a needed condition for approval of the planned link between American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and British Airways Plc.
